utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, madam registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Martinovic and Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. I can hear you very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration with the paper that the usher is going to show you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. President, I have no sound, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you very much. First of all, protective measures. The witness has requested the following protective measures: pseudonym and facial image distortion. The motivation is traditional, reasons of security.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I guess there is no objections. Thank you very much. Your request is granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, your request for protective measures has been granted by the Trial Chamber. Here in the courtroom, you will be called Witness VV. Facial image distortion means that your face will not be seen on the screen or the television. Now, you will be given a sheet of paper and you will see your name there. If everything is all right and the spelling of your name and first name is okay, you may say "yes" without reading it aloud.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, my questions, and I suggest the witness responses, will go mostly to the following parts of the indictment: background, paragraph 7; superior authority, paragraph 14; general allegations, paragraphs 18 through 21; Count 1, paragraph 31, 34, AB; Counts 2 through 5, paragraph 43; Counts 9 through 12, paragraphs 45, 50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness VV, you were born in Mostar municipality 1967; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: In 1993, you lived in the east part of Mostar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And now you live in Mostar; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness VV, in April 1992, you were mobilised with ABiH army with the 4th Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And for some period of time, you were fighting against the Serbs together with the HVO; am I right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber in which part of the front against the Serbs did you fight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: At that time, the front line was in the area of Podvelezje and it was split up between the ABiH and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: What kind of relations existed between the Muslim and Croats then, I mean, first of all, armija and HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: At first, that is in 1992, the relations as far as the regular soldiers were concerned, quite all right. They jointly went together to man the front lines facing the Serb aggressors and there were no problems between the HVO and the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And when did you realise that there was somebody happening between the Croats and Muslims in the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: The first time that I noticed something as a soldier was when I went to visit my family which was in Croatia. I got documents from the 4th Corps that I could go and visit them; however, on the way near Buna, there was a Croatian checkpoint. They turned me back. They said that I could not use these documents, that I had to go to the HVO headquarters and get a paper from them in order to be able to clear the checkpoints. That was in early 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you go to the HVO quarters to get those documents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I did not go because that was very difficult to get into the headquarters as a member of ABiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, I would ask you not to speak too fast because your response will be translated simultaneously into French and B/C/S. Could you recall the Trial Chamber the events that occurred in Mostar in April 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: In April 1993, it was already clear, one could see that the relations between the HVO and the army had become quite tense. The HVO policemen at checkpoints stopped -- were stopping members of the ABiH and provoked them frequently without any reason. They were turning them back. They would not let them pass through to go to wherever their destinations were, and then the sniping provocations started, first, against the members of the ABiH and later against civilians, too. The headquarters of the 2nd battalion of ABiH were in Hotel Mostar and they requested -- they demanded that the headquarters be dislocated and their conflict ensued between the 15th and the 20th April, 1993. The shooting went on for one night, and the next day there was -- there were negotiations between the ABiH commander and the HVO and it was agreed that the 2nd Battalion would be dislocated and moved to the primary school at Alekse Santica. And a relative cease-fire was then observed through early May, however, there was still sniping incidents and provocations on the part of the HVO and people were -- people started being taken from their apartments in the west side of Mostar to the Heliodrome. In other words, families of those men who were members of the ABiH were taken there, and this went on until the 9th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And what happened on the 9th of May, Witness VV? I think the Trial Chamber is well aware of the situation on the 9th of May in the central Mostar. I would like you to recount the Trial Chamber what was happening in the area where your unit was deployed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: On the 9th of May, early in the morning, the HVO carried out an attack against the ABiH, that is, an attack was launched against the east side of Mostar. They first attacked Vranica, where the 4th Corps had its headquarters, and the Konak, where the two units belonging to the 3rd battalion of the 4th Corps were deployed. That was a fierce attack, and between 8.00 and 9.00, I heard an announcement that the white flags should be hoisted and we should surrender and no one would be harmed. However, we did not do this. As a response to these attacks, the ABiH ordered the advance of its troops at Zalik, and during that day, it took Zalik and then maintained it and kept it all through the rest of the war. To the south of Mostar, that is the area of Dracevica and Gnojnica, the ABiH also controlled the territory but where it had the majority Muslim population which were in the HVO uniform but that, too, then, fell to the army. This is what the army undertook as its steps in -- on the 9th of May, Blagaj, Dracevica, Zalik.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Where was your unit deployed because I don't see the name of that location in the transcript? Kornik, or something like that? I don't see it in the transcript

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: It was Konak, K-O-N-A-K. It's the old section of town. That is where the former JNA command post was, that is, until 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Now, Your Honours, I would like the usher to show the witness Exhibit 34.1, Prosecution Exhibit. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, I would like you to take a look at the map and, first of all, indicate the centre of this area Mostar by encircling it and putting number one.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Mostar. Now you may take a marker and circle Mostar and put a number 1 on it. Now, Zalik. Make a bigger ring, please, because it is not seen. Number 2.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would just like to request, when my learned friend asked that the city of Mostar be circled, then perhaps we should really do so, circle the city, because what the gentleman had circled is, I don't know, a street or maybe the old bridge or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Central Mostar. We were talking about Central Mostar and Zalik is a part of Mostar, just south of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we did not understand each other, Your Honours. Everything that you can see there is Mostar and all I asked was if we are going to talk about Mostar, then that is what we should do because what has been circled really does not represent Mostar Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. itself. That is all I wanted to say. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: My learned friend is too fast. I just wanted to ask now the witness what Zalik means in the relation to Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness VV, is Zalik a part of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Zalik is part of Mostar. It is adjacent to the old part of Mostar and the Carina, the customs area, customs zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: So by number one, we mean the central Mostar and number 2, Zalik as a part of Mostar adjacent to the old city.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: You would take -- put aside the map for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: What happened in Mostar on the 30th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: On the 30th of June, 1993, the army was tasked to liberate Bijelo Polje in order to link up with Sarajevo because the population was already without food. There was hunger, people ate one meal a day and it was very poor quality food. On the 30th of June, the army ordered its forces to move on Bijelo Polje. So on the 30th of June, Bijelo Polje was liberated, Rastani, and Sjeverni Logor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Now, usher, I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 11.18.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness VV, I would like you to indicate the northern cap on this map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay, you may put the first letters of your alphabet, "SL." Witness V, to the best of your recollection, which parts of Mostar were under ABiH control after the 30th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: On the 30th of June, 1993, the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina had under its control Bijelo Polje along the Neretva and next -- and at a curve near the convent, the HVO held on the left bank of Neretva the Elementara, but then it went on next to the Carinski bridge to the right on to Santicva. So down Santica Street, down to the intersection where the department store used to be, down the Bulevar to the Ivo Lola Ribar bridge, then again down the Neretva to the Vinerije, to the winery, and then from there to the left from the airport towards Blagaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Could you indicate those points on the map, just show with the pointer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Please, I suggest that the Trial Chamber is waiting for your comments.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: So down the Neretva valley to Carinski bridge, then crossing the Neretva to Alekse Santica Street, and then to the right and towards the intersection where the department store was down the Bulevar, Bulevar still, Bulevar all the way down to Ivo Lola Ribar bridge to Tekija, and then following the Neretva once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Now you may put aside this map and just lay on the ELMO map 34.10.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Now, I would like the witness to just -- you mentioned Rastani as a village that was regained on the 30th of June. Could you indicate it on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Now, please encircle it and put number 3.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: So by number 3, we understand Rastani. And Bijelo Polje, I would like you to do the same with Bijelo Polje area, just encircle. It should be a big ring because this area seem to be bigger. And you may put number 4.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Now you may put aside map 34.10.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness VV, and who was in control of Bijelo Polje area before the 30th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Before the 30th of June, the HVO units held the Bijelo Polje and -- but at that time, the HVO helped gather both Muslims and Croats until the 30th of June. And on the 30th of June when the army joined in, the Muslims joined the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and as of the 30th of June right up to this day, Bijelo Polje is under the control of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And who was in command of the HVO unit deployed in Bijelo Polje area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: The HVO units deployed in Bijelo Polje were commanded by Mr. Marko Radic, called Maka.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you personally know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I knew personally Mr. Marko Radic. On a number of occasions, we were together and once I was even in the headquarters at Bijelo Polje, that is, in his office. It was in 1992, at the time when the operation against the Serb Montenegrin aggressor in the area of Podvelezje was under preparation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, to the best of your knowledge, what kind of forces did ABiH have in Rastani after the 30th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: After the 30th of June, the BH army had between 30 and 40 soldiers in Rastani plus Rastani villagers, I mean Muslim Rastani villagers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And what about the Bijelo Polje? I mean the same question, what kind of troops were deployed there, the number?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: About 120 men of the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina were in Bijelo Polje, plus the population which had moved over to the side of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina after the 30th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Where was your unit deployed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Our unit was deployed at Vrapcici and we met the line between the hydropower plant and the area above the Djuro Salaj Factory before Elementara.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: How far away is Vrapcici from Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: About 7 or 8 kilometres, that is, up to the first houses in Vrapcici. That is from the board which says, "You are now leaving Mostar" to the first houses in Vrapcici, it's about 7 or 8 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you participate in any military operations in June/July 1993 in the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: No, I did not participate in that operation because I was wounded on the 1st of July by an HVO shell in the locality of Vrapcici and I was transferred to the hospital at Carina, where I was receiving treatment right up until the 15th of September. On the 15th of September, I rejoined my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, is it correct that on the 24th of August, the HVO regained Rastani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: On the 24th of August, 1993, the HVO took over Rastani again, and on that occasion, a number of civilians, that is Rastani villagers, were killed but I do not know which HVO unit took part in that fighting and who was their commander because at that time I was receiving treatment so that I did not have that kind of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness VV, it's also a fact well known that on the 20th of September, ABiH tried to recapture Rastani. Did you participate in that operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: On the 20th of September, 1993, the BH army liberated Rastani, but I was not taking part because I had not been reactivated fully yet, that is, I was involved with logistics, I would supply food ammunitions, and so on and so forth. So I did not participate in the operation on the 20th of September in that fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: But did you go to the battle area on the 20th of September?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: On the 20th of September, 1993, when the BH army liberated Rastani, I did not go to Rastani. I was in Vrapcici that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Trial Chamber how far away is Vrapcici from Rastani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: There is -- the river Neretva flows between Vrapcici and Rastani so they are very close.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you go ever to Rastani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: The first time I went to Rastani was on the 22nd of September in the morning, and I returned to Vrapcici in the evening, so on the evening of the 22nd of September I was back in Vrapcici.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: But what was happening on the 22nd of September in Rastani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: On the 22nd of September, in the afternoon, the HVO attempted to recapture Rastani, to put it again under its control. However, on the 22nd, they did not succeed in doing that. That is right up until the 23rd, Rastani remained under the BH army control.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And do you know in which area of Rastani were ABiH soldiers deployed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: The soldiers of the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina were deployed from the fly-over on the way to Mostar following the upper houses on the way to Raska Gora all the way up to the hydropower plant Mostar 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did they have a sort of headquarters in Rastani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: There was no command in Rastani except that a low-ranking officer who was commanding the troops in the field also commanded there, but the command of that unit was in Vrapcici.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did they have communication, radio communication?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes, there was a radio communication between the headquarters and the commander who was in Rastani.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: You just told the Trial Chamber that on the 22nd of September, you were in Rastani. For what purposes did you go there? It was the 22nd of September, I repeat.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: On the 22nd of September, they sent me to get food and some ammunition for the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, so that I Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. crossed the Neretva in a boat in the early morning hours. That was in the area of Sutina, in the area of Sutina, and since the HVO was controlling it, that is, they had a good overview from Raska Gora, we had to do it very early in the morning or in the evening if you wanted to cross the Neretva to Rastani, or the other way around to Vrapcici.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And where did you find BH soldiers in Rastani on the 22nd of September?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: A group of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was in the Silo and another group was to the right towards the dam, that is, in the houses where the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina were having their meals.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you go to Rastani on the 23rd of September?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: On the 23rd of September, around 10.00 in the morning, my commander woke me up and told me that there was fighting in Rastani and that ammunition had to be taken there to support the BH army, so that he woke me and my colleague up. And we, with the commander, we went to the headquarters. We took a crate of ammunition, some 1200 bullets, 7.62 millimetre, and split it in two halves, put it in our rucksacks and through Vrapcici and Suhi Dol, down Sutina, crossed the river by boat and on our way, he pointed to me in the direction of Dumpor's houses and told me, "This is where our men are." So my task was to get there to Dumpor's houses and take ammunition to our men down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like just to go into private session for some minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Usher, I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit P34.10. It's on the desk.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness VV, what I will ask you now just to show the route you took from Vrapcici to Rastani on the 23rd of September and just mark it with a dotted line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Could you show it because I'm sorry, I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Could you put a thicker line, a little bit, because ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And just put an arrow in the end of this line leading to Rastani.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And put number 5.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: You may put aside the exhibit for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: So Witness VV, you have just told us that your commander gave you an assignment to get to Dumpor houses; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Had you ever been in that area before the 23rd of September, I mean Dumpor house area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: But did you understand from his instructions where that area was located in Rastani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: From his instruction, I gathered that these houses were to the right from the elecktroprenos, from the electric transmission grid towards Raska there and one could see those houses very well from Vrapcici where we were quartered.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: At what time did you leave Rastani -- Vrapcici for Rastani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Sometime between 10.00 and 11.00, thereabouts. I cannot confirm it because we had no watches, and the shelling was very intensive.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: What did you observe in Rastani on reaching it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: In Rastani, we observed very thick smoke, and later on, I saw that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. it was houses burning and very intensive shelling, perhaps the most intensive shelling in the Mostar area in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: How long did it take you to get to Rastani? I'm sorry, I mean to the area of Dumpor houses.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: About 3.00, that is, from Vrapcici to Rastani, we used the damaged houses, those that had already burnt down, to find the cover from the shelling, so that it was around 3.00 that we made it to Dumpor's houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And how did you move around Rastani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: In Rastani, we separated, that is, in a single file, 10 to 15 metres apart, to reach the house or a tree or something, take cover there, wait for the other one to arrive, and then move on. And that is how we -- and when we arrived, when we got to Dumpor's houses, we hid in a cellar. That house had burnt down a long time before that and that is where we spent a certain period of time, in the cellar of that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Usher, I would like you to show the witness Exhibit P34.2.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Please take a close look at this map, and perhaps you will find Dumpor houses area in the map. If you can do that, please, show that area to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. Could you encircle this area and put letter D, which will mean Dumpor.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. You may put this exhibit aside.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: So Witness VV, did you find ABiH soldiers in Dumpor houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: We did not find ABiH soldiers there because they had already withdrawn from the Dumpor's houses to the right towards the power station, power plant.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: But on your way from Vrapcici to Rastani, did you have any communication with ABiH soldiers who were deployed in Rastani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: On our way from Vrapcici to Rastani, we had no communication either with the soldiers who were at Rastani nor with our headquarters which stayed at Vrapcici. So we had no radio communications nor any other communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. Did you try to look for army of soldiers in Rastani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I previously said that at Dumpor's houses we took cover in a cellar, in a basement, because the shelling was very intense and we spent there a short period of time, not very long. Then the shelling moved away. We came out, and we went from Dumpor's houses to Punji houses - there were only three there - up from Dumpor's houses, and as I got there, I saw three or four civilians and behind them, 10 or 15 soldiers who were -- had fanned out. At first I did not understand, I didn't realise who these soldiers were but they started shouting at us to surrender, and then we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: But what was your perception, what were those soldiers, civilians, doing and HVO soldiers in the area, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: When they started shouting at us to surrender, I realised that these soldiers had taken part in the fighting, but at first I did not understand where the civilians came from, so that I was fairly confused and at that point I did not know what unit this was until I was captured. I did not know who the unit was until I was captured and then I recognised Kolobara and Splico. At that point, Kolbara doused me with gasoline. He -- and he started as if he was going to torch me, and in one hand, he held a Motorola. Somebody called him on the Motorola. At that point, he stepped back, talked to him, and then told his soldiers that the prisoners had to be taken alive to Siroki Brijeg because the old man had ordered so. They had insignia. They were clear and I recognised them. I could see clearly that they were the Convicts Battalion. I saw clearly that they were the soldiers that belonged to the Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Now, Witness, let's stop here, I would like to clarify some issues now. You just told that you recognised some of the soldiers and named Kolbara and Splico. Did you know those persons before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Before that, Splico was with HOS, and he used to wear a black uniform and when the HOS, the HOS was dissolved, he transferred to the Convicts Battalion, but I personally never was associated with him, never socialised but I did see him in town. He was about 185 centimetres tall, quite thin, and he was always in the black uniform so he was easily recognisable.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: But did you see him before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I did see him before the HVO and the ABiH conflict but I never socialised with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: When did you see him? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: In the period during 1992 when the ABiH and the HVO jointly defended the area against the Serbian and Montenegrin aggressors. I may have seen him two or three times, I don't recall exactly, but during that year, I saw him two or three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And now about Kolbara, how did you learn his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: In November 1992, when an offensive against the Serb Montenegrin aggressor at Podvelezje was being prepared, Mato Radic sent two soldiers to the Konak to get me and another soldier. They came to the Konak to get the two of us and we went over to the headquarters, and we sat down with Mario, called Diko Skobic, and the two soldiers who had come to get us. And through a conversation, we learned that the Convicts Battalion was taking part in the operations against the Serb Montenegrin aggressors in the area of Podvelezje, around Konak. And then I asked Diko, whom I knew -- I knew a number of Croats from Vrapcici. I knew Sesar, Kolobara Skobic and other Croats who lived in Vrapcici; we were close. I asked Mario whether there was anyone in the Convicts Battalion whom I knew and he said that Kolbara was one of them, and I asked him how he was and he said the same -- the same, Kolbara, nicknamed "Droba." He said he's always been. And Mario and Droba and I a number of times had drinks together. So at the moment when I was captured, I first saw Droba, and when I looked closer, the other man was a better build than Droba, short hair, but quite strong looking young man. So I had never seen him before but I recognised him by those features. And when I was transferred to Ljubuski later, when I was in the camp at Ljubuski, about ten days into my stay at Ljubuski when we were going out for lunch, I saw Kolbara standing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. We will return to this topic later on. And do you know -- sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We have to make a break. We will resume at ten past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, on behalf of interpreters, I would ask you not to speak too fast, they cannot catch you. All right? And now, I would like to clarify some issues from your previous testimony, I mean just a passage of testimony. You mentioned a person whose full name was Radic. What was his first name, because I see some inconsistencies in the transcript?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Marko Radic, nicknamed "Maka."

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you. And let's return to this Droba. Did you know his first name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I don't know his first name. All his friends called him Drobo so I never knew the name. We did have -- sit down around the table and drank coffee or beer together, and I always knew him as Drobo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you know to which unit he belonged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I don't know exactly which unit, but he was under Marko Radic's command, so that was the unit from Bijelo Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And do you know the name of the second Kolobara whom you met in Rastani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: When we were sitting at Marko Radic's, Mario Skobic told me that Marinko Kolobara, who was the member of the Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Could you describe him, just to the best of your recollection, when you saw him first in 1993? I mean in Rastani.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Kolobara was shortish, 170 to 175, well-built, broad shouldered. His hair was cut short and he was -- he had his -- he had fair hair, and he was around 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: You've just told the Trial Chamber what Kolobara was doing in respect to you and what was happening to your colleague at that time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: They cursed and they verbally abused both my colleague and me. They kicked us with their boots, and they hit us with their rifle butts. They also punched us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you see any other people in Rastani apart from HVO soldiers at the moment when you were captured and shortly after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: At the moment when I was captured, I saw three or four civilians walking in front of these soldiers. I remember well one young man, he had sneakers and jeans and a T-shirt. At dusk. When we were led out of Rastani behind a silo, we saw civilians collecting the bodies of killed soldiers and also collecting the wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And now I would like to direct you to this Motorola conversation. You just told the Trial Chamber that Kolobara was talking about some old man who had ordered to take people to Siroki Brijeg. Did you understand what old man was meant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: At that point, I did not know to whom this word "old man," referred, but later on when I was locked up in the cellar, I learned from these soldiers in reference to Mladen Naletilic, Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Which cellar do you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: In Siroki Brijeg at the headquarters. In Mladen Naletilic's headquarters, we were in the cellar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: We will return to the subject a little bit later. How long did you stay in Rastani on the 23rd of September?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: We stayed in Rastani until the early evening, dusk. Then they took us to Bakina Luka, that was in the city. And just before this underground passage, we encountered these soldiers which had the HV insignia. That was the shift which was going to take over the shift at the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: How many soldiers did you see, I mean, with HV insignia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: It was early evening, but there were a lot of them, about 50. They were walking in single file, one after another.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: How long did they keep you in Bakina Luka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: A van was waiting for us there. We did not stay there at Bakina Luka. They loaded us in the van and took us to Siroki Brijeg right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Had you ever been in Siroki Brijeg before the 23rd of September?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I was in Siroki Brijeg in 1990, but only passing through. In other words, I did not stop there. So it is only now that I first got to know the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And where did they take you to in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: When we entered Siroki Brijeg, we crossed the bridge and went to the right about a hundred metres from the bridge. We got off there, and they walked us into a building. I thought that that was either the Obnova or the tobacco station.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Could you describe that building to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I cannot describe it because it was already dark, and straight from the van they took us to the office, where they continued to abuse and beat us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you see your colleague at that moment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: He stayed back in the hallway, and I was led into the office, in the office in that building, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: In what condition was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: We were already bloodied, and we had swellings. Our eyes were already swollen and closing, getting shut from all the beatings that we had received. So we were not in a good shape. And after awhile, they took us back to the van and took us to the civilian prison in Siroki Brijeg where they locked us up individually. I was locked up in one cell and my colleague was locked up in another.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Now, usher, I would like you to show Witness VV Exhibit number 26.4.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness VV, do you recognise the building depicted in this picture?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I recognise the building. This is the prison where we were brought late that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And what happened to you that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: That night they locked us up, the soldiers who had brought us there, and they left. After awhile, five or six soldiers entered my cell, and they first started to insult and provoke me. Then one of the soldiers threw a lighter down on the floor of the cell and told me to pick it up. When I bent to pick it up, he hit me. He actually kicked me. And then the rest of the soldiers started beating me, and I fell down. They continued to beat me. They continued to beat me until a policeman on duty entered and said, "Leave the man alone. He's not going to survive." Then they left and entered the cell where my colleague was and continued to beat and mistreat him. I could hear moans coming from the other room. That went on for about half an hour and then they left. We spent the night there, and in the morning around 7.00 or 8.00, soldiers again came in, four or five of them. They took us back to that building where we had been the previous night, that is, the first building where we were taken to when we came to Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, just a moment. Just a moment. Do you know to which unit the soldiers who were beating you in MUP station belonged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Those soldiers belonged to the Convicts Battalion because they had patches on the left sleeve, and it clearly displayed the Convicts Battalion insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: So they took you to -- to the previous building, and what happened there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: They locked us up there in the basement. There was a tin partition wall there. My colleague was placed behind that metal partition, and I was placed in front of it, and then they left. After awhile, a man walked in and told me, "Come with me." He took me to an Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. office, and I saw in the office, behind the desk, Mr. Mladen Naletilic, Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, not too fast, please, not too fast. Just some minutes ago in your testimony and now, you mentioned a person, Mladen Naletilic, Tuta. Had you ever seen him before September 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: As far as Mr. Mladen Naletilic, Tuta, is concerned, I first saw him in 1992 in Posvelezje, in the area of Sipovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Could you give us a little bit of details of that meeting with Mladen Naletilic, Tuta, in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I personally did not meet with him, but I was in the unit, and he arrived at Sipovac, where he visited with our commander at that time and discussed the situation there because he was at Posvelezje.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you know what position he occupied at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: At that time, he was the commander of the Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you see him in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I did see him in the area of Sipovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Could you describe him, to the best of your recollection, how he looked like at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: He was about 60 years old, long hair, eyeglasses with lenses, and fairly grey.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: So was it the same person that you saw at the desk in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes, that was the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did he speak to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: He did. He called a girl, ordered tea for me and coffee for himself, and asked me, "Who harmed you? Who hurt you?" And I shrugged my shoulders because I didn't know the name of the person, and I was too afraid to speak out. And he said that nobody would harm me again, that I was his prisoner. And after we finished, well, coffee and tea, he called somebody by the name of Bosanac and that guy came and took me back to the cellar, and that's the only time that I saw Tuta at Siroki.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did he ask you any other questions apart from your physical condition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: All he asked me was about the whereabouts of our commanders, and I answered, and that was the only thing that Mr. Tuta asked me about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you give response to his questions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I told him where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And did they beat you after this conversation with Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: For the first 12 days, they would come in several times a day, four or five soldiers, and beat me with their boots, and belts, fists, and a soldier came in with a crutch and also beat me with a crutch and his hands and his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: You just mentioned that one of the soldiers was called or had his name Bosanac. Did he beat you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: He beat me, and every time that those soldiers, four or five of them came in, he was with them invariably and when he said, "Enough. No more," they would stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you know to which unit he belonged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: The Convicts Battalion, because we were in the headquarters of the Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And what was happening to your colleague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: My colleague sustained severe beating in the prison where we slept so that in the morning, he could not walk, and one of the Croatian soldiers ordered me to help him and I took him by his hand and -- into the cellar and there he was locked. And he was left alone during those 12 days while we were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did anyone from HVO commanders visit you in Siroki Brijeg prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: On the seventh day of imprisonment, it was visited by Mr. Marko Radic, called Maka, and greeted me, told me not to worry, that I would be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did he interrogate you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: All he asked me was about two members of the HVO who had beforehand, when Rastani was in the hands of the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, tried to mine the hydropower plant, but they failed to do that. But after that incident, all we heard was an explosion, and two or three days later, downstream from the hydropower plant in the Neretva, we found a body in the diving gear, in the diving suit, and I told Mr. Marko Radic that we had found only one body and he said that there had to be two of them. But we found only one body, and it was to Mostar where it was identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Now, were you exchanged according to Marko Radic promise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: No, I was exchanged only on the 19th of March after the agreement on cease-fire had been reached between the HVO and the army of Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. And were there any other prisoners in Siroki Brijeg prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Personally, I did not see other prisoners, but on the 16th of November when we were transferred from Siroki to Ljubuski, as we were waiting for the busses to be taken to Ljubuski, one of the Croatian soldiers said that other prisoners should be brought in to clean the cellar where we had been kept, and that is how I realised that there were more prisoners apart from us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: What about the conditions of your detention in Tobacco Station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: The conditions were very poor. We received food every two or three days, and that would be a quarter of a loaf of bread and a small 100-gram tin of pate, no water at all, so that we rinsed our mouths with urine.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did they take you into the open air?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: No, they did not take us into open air except the day when we were transferred to Ljubuski, except that on the twelfth day, I was taken to the office by Bosanac, a General, and another member of the Convicts Battalion. They put me at a desk there and put wires from an induction telephone, and they fixed them to my fingers and then turned the handle of the telephone so as to pass the current from my fingers to my toes, and it lasted between half an hour and an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Could you describe Bosanac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Bosanac was between 175 and 180 centimetres tall, strongly built, fair, short hair, not more than 25 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And could you describe the other person who was called or nicknamed "General"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: The General was 180, 185 centimetres tall, black hair, thin, somewhere between 25 and 30 years of age.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you know to which unit he belonged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: The Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Well, every time they came, they talked, and I overheard from their conversation between them that they called him a general, because between them -- I mean, they used their nicknames addressing one another so that I do not know any of their real names. But from those overheard conversations, I know that the fair-haired one was Bosanac and that this other one's nickname was "General" and that they were members of the Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Were you ever registered by the Red Cross when you were kept in Siroki Brijeg detention facility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: So when were you transferred to Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: On the 16th of November they took us out of the cellar. There were about 10 or 15 soldiers who ill-treated us, who teased us, brought a newspaper with the photograph of the destroyed old bridge and insulted us. And then two cars arrived, one Golf and one Mercedes, and put me in the boot of the Mercedes and my colleague was put in the boot of the Golf, and that is how they transferred us to Ljubuski. I mean, we were both in the boots of the two cars, in the trunks of the two cars.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Were you registered by the Red Cross in Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: In Ljubuski we were registered by the Red Cross on the 26th of November. That was when they came there the first time. They took down our particulars. And on the 29th of November, they brought us those Red Cross cards.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And what about the conditions of your detention in Ljubuski camp before the registration by the Red Cross and after?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Before we were registered by the Red Cross, my colleague and I were put in a cell without any blankets or sponge mattresses or anything. I mean, we had to lie down on the bare floor. We had food every second day until we were registered by the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did anything happen after the registration?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: After the registration by the Red Cross, they put us together with other prisoners who were there, and there were about 80 prisoners there, members of the BH army, police, and political prisoners, that is, those who were members of the party.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask you just to go into private session for some minutes now not to reveal the identity of some people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And how did they treat prisoners there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: The prisoners, about eight of us, all went to work except myself, my colleague, and a few of high-ranking political figures. All the others went to work every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Why didn't they take you to work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I wouldn't know, but the first time, I was taken to work after the truce was signed, that is, a few days before the exchange, and I went to Caritas to load and unload goods.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Were Muslim prisoners the only ones who were kept in Ljubuski prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: No. There were HVO prisoners too, but they were in another wing, and their cells were open so that in daytime they could walk around the compound, around the prison compound. One of them had the keys to our cells, and he locked us up and opened it and on a number of occasions he ill-treated me, beat me, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you know his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Mile Kordic, nicknamed Tuta, nicknamed Pop.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you know why he had such kind of nicknames?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Well, not exactly, but prisoners used to say that he was a member of the Convicts Battalion, and they called him Pop because he -- which means "priest," because he had allegedly killed a priest and that that was why he was in detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, somewhere in the beginning of the examination-in-chief, you just told me that you saw Kolobara again in Ljubuski prison. Could you now recount the story?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Well, when we came out with other prisoners for breakfast for the first time, or lunch, we -- the prisoners of Croat ethnicity were standing in a circle at the place where we were eating and at that moment I recognised Kolobara, but I held my head down. And he recognised us, too, and approached and spilled our lunch, took us back to the cell and there he ill-treated and beat us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Was it the same Kolobara that you had seen in Rastani in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes, that same Kolobara.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Usher, now, I would like you to show Witness VV Exhibit P677. Madam Registrar, I suggest that we have enough copies of the documents for the Judges.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes -- sorry, but maybe they are in the binders. Then I would ask the usher to place this document on the ELMO, the English version first. Unfortunately, I cannot see it well. The image is very blurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, do you have the B/C/S version of the document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like you to take a look at it and tell me if you see any names which are familiar to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: No. No. These names I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I mean not only first name, but full names as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the question was quite clear. The witness spent a long time studying the document and he said he did not know the names of the witness. He has answered this question after a very long and thorough study of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, don't you see the names that are familiar to you? If you don't, you don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness has already answered and we didn't even object to this document. You see, we kept silent all the time. I do not see what does this document have to do with this witness, but I didn't want to ask my learned friend that because the Chamber should hear and see as much as possible. I think it is very good for the Defence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe that the witness answered the question by saying, "No, these names I do not know."

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, you may put aside the document. Now, Witness, I would like to ask you some questions about Splico. Do you know his real name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I don't, because everybody called him Splico and even in -- around town, he was referred to as Splico, somebody in a black uniform, and that was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you know why he was nicknamed Splico?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Well, my guess is that he came from Split, and that that was why he was called Splico.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Now, I would like usher to show Witness VV document Exhibit 538.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, I would like you just to read the first line of the document after the word "Izvor."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness said that he did not know the name of the person nicknamed Splico. So may I ask what is the purpose of showing this document to suggest that this was Splico when the witness, a moment ago, said that he did not know the name of this person named Splico, and Splico is only a nickname.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prosecutor, would you please shed some light on this issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think that I don't propose anything unlawful or strange. We have a document in our domain where some name, some nickname is mentioned, and perhaps we have some other documents. Why can't we do some investigation here in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know if the purpose of our being here is to investigate. Again, I may be held for not knowing enough about the common law practice, but it is very easy to state that any person that is from Split could be named Splico. I am not going to object to this document, and if the Prosecution does not tender it, the Defence will tender it, but you cannot use this document to suggest to this witness here that the person nicknamed Splico has this name because he said that he did not know his name. So that is not fair.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, let us see what is the following questions that the Prosecutor will ask. I don't think that his question was only about the names, especially that nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: My question was just to read the first line of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honours, my apologies. I wouldn't rise to object, but this is the system that we're following. It's very clear that the first line contains the name of this person, and despite my objection, my learned friend is exactly doing what I objected to - and my apologies if I use this expression, but we are not children here - after the witness had said that he did not know the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We understand that the witness said clearly that he only knows this man's nickname but not the real name. We understand that. We just want to know what the questions that the Prosecutors will follow. We can make our own judgement at a later stage according to the cross-examination -- the direct examination and the cross-examination on this very issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my learned friend asked three times what is contained in the first line of, and this is why I objected to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But there is no answer from this witness. We would like to hear what this witness is going to answer to this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the word "Splico" in this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I do. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Please, maybe you can read the first lines of the document where you see this name Splico.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: "Vedran Bijuk, called Splico."

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Date of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Born on 26 September 1957 in Split, Croatia -- Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you. You may put aside this document for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies. I do not want to belabour this, but was this the question and was this the answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prosecutor, I think you should ask this witness whether he's sure that the nickname Splico, with his real name, is that name on the document or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: The witness explained that he does not know his real name, but I think that we have some documents that can shed some light on the person whose name is Vedran Bijuk, nicknamed Splico.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, there may be many people who have got the nickname Splico in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it's quite possible, but why I'm proposing all the things is because I've got some more documents at my disposal that I hope would help you to make a decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may try that, but I'm not quite sure about the results.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I'm in your hands, Your Honour. Thank you. Now I would ask usher to show the Witness VV Exhibit number P614.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, I would like you to take a look at the second paragraph of this document and read it closely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Could you place the document to the ELMO, I mean an English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, have you read the document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Not yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if this is the investigation that is now being conducted by my learned friend, I can say the least is that it is not fair. What does this document have to do with this -- this witness have to do with this document? I don't understand. What is the witness supposed to say here? What kind of evidence should he give here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That's just what we want to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, why I propose this document because this document, again, has one name mentioned in it which is linked to the previous document. I mean the name is linked to the previous document. That's why I asked the witness if he can see the name Vedran Bijuk in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness never mentioned that first and last name. The witness never mentioned any first and last names. He mentioned one nickname. If this is not suggestive -- he is tormenting the witness to tell him what he wants to hear. I ask that he not be allowed to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prosecutor, it seems that we'll get nowhere by reading those documents at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: At this moment maybe we are nowhere, but finally we'll come to some point, I suggest, if you allow me to continue with my investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'll let you go for a while, but I hope you could arrive at that point as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I will do my best. It will take me some minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: So, Witness, do you see the name Vedran Bijuk in this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Could you read some other names mentioned just along with this name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Please read them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Vlado Anic, Mario Drmac, and Drago Klemo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And thank you. And now I would like you to go to page 2 of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can I ask something? Would my learned friend be so kind to provide us a copy? We have 17 binders. It is difficult for us to carry everything. If you have -- they're always very kind and provide us all the copies, but right now we're caught without one. If we can just get a spare copy, we would be most grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I am not sure, I am not sure that we have spare Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. copies of this document, because it was before in one of the binders. We have provided you with all the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. We did receive it. That's not what I said. However, we have a trolley with 17 binders there, but we did not bring it to the courtroom, and we were not advised that this document was going to be used. Otherwise, you always very kindly let us know in advance what you are going to use. So what I suggest is perhaps we can put on the ELMO so we can all view it. I apologise for this intervention.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes. Usher, if you could help us to put the English version -- the Croatian version. Sorry. Do you need -- does the counsel need an English version or a B/C/S version on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The B/C/S, because of our clients, so that our clients can actually follow and see which documents are being discussed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: It's not seen. Page 1 first. We were talking about page 1. Will you move it up a little bit because the most interesting place is not seen. Stop here. The seventh line from the upper side of the second paragraph. And now I would ask you to go to page 2 of the same document of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like you to leaf through the document, Witness VV, and tell me if you see any name which is familiar to you. To make things easier, I think it will be the third paragraph from the bottom. Have you read it, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you see any name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Which name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Milenko Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Milenko Kordic. Do you mean that Milenko Kordic that you saw in Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the translation, we heard whether the witness thinks that this was the person that he saw in Ljubuski; in other words, it calls for pure speculation. We're in your hands. I indeed do not know what the purpose of showing this document to the witness is. If the witness is asked whether he thinks that this was the person whom he had seen in Ljubuski, I think that that is improper form for asking this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let's hear the answer from this witness first.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, do you see any information relevant to Milenko Kordic in the brackets here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: As I read this, I noticed that I am linking this name with the person in Ljubuski because even the persons who were ethnic Croats told me that he had killed a priest there and this, in my mind, creates a link between this person and the one that I see here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't have any questions in respect of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness said that the -- the witness said that he could not link -- that he could not link person with the -- where what the witness has said, in other words, no linkage between this name and the person whom he knew in Ljubuski. I can do it in the cross, but I mean that was the answer that we all heard as a response to what the Prosecutor said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what's the problem, but from the transcript, I see that "I notice that I am linking this name to this person in Ljubuski," this is just an opposite. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, but the witness ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I consulted with my colleague to -- the witness stated very clearly on the basis of the document, he does -- did not link what he read in the document with the person whom he met at Ljubuski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prosecutor, would you ask the question again and make it clear for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, in the transcript we have, "I noticed that I'm linking this name with the person in Ljubuski." Was your response entered into the transcript correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: According to the stories which I heard in the prison by the HVO members who were imprisoned there and members of the ABiH who were imprisoned there, that name does link it, in other words, I think that it is one and the same person. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, on the last document, with your leave to be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think we have to have our break. We will resume at quarter to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Now I would like usher to show Witness VV Exhibit number P704. And since the B/C/S version doesn't have pages, I direct you to ERN 00795361, 00795361, English version page 9. Could you put the B/C/S version on the ELMO. I would like to check if they are on the same page. Yes. Yes. You can give it back to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness VV, I would like you to read very closely --

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Sorry? You don't have the exhibit? It's an old exhibit. 704.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, have you read it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: What do you see in front of you? What is this document called?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. What do you see in the letterhead of this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if this is still part of the investigation that is being conducted which you allowed, I again don't understand what link did three documents that the Prosecutor has presented make to what this witness has stated so far. He has stated that he did not know any names, and now he's asking him to read some headings, some names, even though the witness has stated that he did not know any. I had asked in advance and you allowed it. I respect that. But I think that all these questions should be disallowed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, we understand that this witness already mentioned some names during his testimony. The question is whether the names on the list are related to the name the witness mentioned in his testimony. I'll let Mr. Prosecutor go for a while. Your objection was correctly recorded in the transcript. We quite understand your concern in this point, but we'll see where the Prosecutor is leading us to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes. I asked the witness just to read the letterhead of the document, to let him understand what kind of document he has in front of him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, Croatian Defence Council, Defence Department, Combat Group 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: My question will be: Witness VV, do you see the name under number 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Under number 6?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Under number 7?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Under number 8?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And there is one name in handwriting at the bottom of the list. Can you read it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Could you read it, please, aloud?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Vlado Anic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. My question will be the last question for today. When were you released from Ljubuski prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: On 19 March 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: This is the end of my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have all seen this document, and we could see that the witness saw some names and we too, but we did not hear a question from the Prosecutor regarding this document nor did we get an answer, which means that the Prosecutor has no questions, he merely wanted to show this document or what?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prosecutor, you may answer the question put forward by the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: My question was quite simple, and it is stemming from the document, Exhibit P614. Some of the names were also mentioned in that document and they were read out by the same witness some minutes before, and I think that any further questions at this point are redundant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any cross-examination? Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecutor turn off his mike, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, I will now undertake the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness VV. Let me introduce myself. I'm one of the counsel for the accused Mladen Naletilic, and I will be asking you some questions. I always warn every witness and I will do so with you, too, bear in mind two things: number one, that we both speak the same language, and I am afraid I am a fast talker and I see that you are quite fast, too. So that I will try to keep myself under control and will you do the same thing, please? In other words, do not start answering before you hear the end of my question. My second thing is I will try to put -- I always try to put my questions as concisely and as briefly as possible and I will welcome your answers in the same vein, thank you very much. Now, my first question to you will be: Have you ever heard of the name Vedran Bijuk, and do you know who that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Counsel, sir, I said in my testimony that I did not remember that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know who is Miroslav Kolobara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Sir, I never met Mr. Miroslav Kolobara but I've heard of his existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, I really -- yes, I have to slow down. Thank you. I had to ask you this because of this document which the Prosecutor showed you on two occasions, requesting an answer from you, but you said in advance that is quite true that you did not know them. That was the reason for my question, but thank you very much for your answers. Let us now move on. And Witness, I deeply sympathise with you and all that you suffered in the area of Siroki Brijeg, but please understand that I have to ask you some questions, so will you please try to be cooperative. I have to cover this area through my cross-examination. I believe you understand my standpoint, don't you? So to begin with, I'd like to ask you if you remember a statement which you gave on the 7th of April, 1997 to the Agency for Investigation and Documentation Mostar sector; it is that famous AID, the secret police. Do you remember that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
