utterances.text: Sir, I gave two statements. On both occasions, investigators from The Hague Tribunal were present.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer, too. So if I understood you properly, at the time when you were making a statement on the 7th of April, 1997 at the AID premises, the investigators of this Tribunal were also present, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I do not know whether I was at the AID, I really don't know, but I know that investigators from The Hague were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Usher, can you please help me. I'd like you to have this statement in front of you so will the usher please help me to get it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You can read above, you can see what this document says where the statement was given.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Mostar sector, but it says the Agency for Investigation and Documentation, abbreviation "AID" Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So it is on their premises that you made this statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I really don't know. I really --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you please then turn to the last page because we also had different kinds of experience here so I want to check it. Is this your signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: This one, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will the counsel and witness please break between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask you, Witness VV, if you will be so kind as to turn to page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I want to ask you, Witness VV, can you really affirm with certainty where is it in Siroki Brijeg that you were, apart from the police station, which you identified today? Can you really state with any confidence, can you say it to this Honourable Court and to yourself where is it were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Sir, in my statement, I said that at the entrance of Siroki Brijeg we crossed the bridge, we turned right, and about a hundred metres further on. So I did not claim anything. I assumed that it could be either Obnova or the tobacco station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Right. So we can do it together. Let us read the last statement on page three. And this is what you say literally: [as read] "I'm not sure where the offices of Tuta's command -- where the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. premises of Tuta's headquarters are. That is, I do not know who the premises belong to. As far as I could see, they were -- they belonged to a socially owned enterprise possibly of the Obnova enterprise, that is, Obnova factory, or the tobacco station." Now, my question to you is, Witness, you are not sure, as a matter of fact, where is it that you were. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: But I said that we arrived there late at night, that we had been badly beaten. Mr. Tuta saw me in the morning with my eyes shut, so that at that time I couldn't really say that with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In other words, you cannot say positively which is -- which are the buildings that you were kept in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I think I said that in 1990, I believe, I went through Siroki Brijeg, and it is a small place. You surely know it. And it was roughly -- I said it was either the socially owned company, which was then Obnova. And these are rather large buildings, and that is why I assumed that that must be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Witness VV, you said today that it was when you saw the soldiers that you inferred that it should be Tuta's command, isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, then, tell us now what kind of insignia did they have. You indicated your left arm. Will you please tell us what kind of emblem did the soldiers have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: At that moment, considering the state I was in and after all this time, it is very difficult to describe it. But as far as my memory serves me, it said in small lettering the "Convicts Battalion," as far as I can recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness VV, thank you. And once again, I apologise to you for making you go once again through -- making you relive once again the situation, which must be very painful. But please understand that somehow we have to do that, because I have some more questions with which I'd like to help this Court and all of us for the sake of the truth. Tell us, did you see that that emblem could -- was a velcro emblem, that is, that it could be taken off and put on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I cannot answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And did you notice anything else on this emblem except --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I just said clearly that these emblems were visible, so that I can affirm that they -- that they were soldiers of Mr. Naletilic. But as for emblems, I really can't tell you more because it was a long time ago. And considering what I had to live through, I really wish that nobody of any ethnicity would have to go through that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I merely wanted to ask you: Did you spot anything else on these emblems apart from these words?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Well, there was some sign, some emblem there, but I can't remember. I know that underneath those words there was also some kind of an emblem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you then concluded that they were members of the Convicts Battalion because of that sign?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Well, it said so. I'm telling you that is what the word said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. I see. Excuse me, but I have to ask you that. And had they had something else, if it said the "1st Brigade," then your conclusion would be that they were of the 1st -- that they were the 1st Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Well, I guess so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, do you know how many units are there at Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please -- and what did the police wear? Were their uniforms black, blue?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: You mean the police in the prison where we spent the night?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I mean the police at Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Sir, the police had blue uniforms, dark, with caps. As a matter of fact, we used to call them railwaymen's uniforms. I think you understand what I mean. They had those caps with the shield there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, Witness VV, of course I understand, but all we are doing here, we are doing it for this Honourable Court, and the Honourable Court has to understand also, so please be patient. So they wore uniforms of policemen of Herceg-Bosna. We can put it that way, can't we, the official one, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did they interrogate you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Nobody asked you any questions, none of the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: No, except that a policeman entered and told them to let me be, and that was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, do you -- are you aware of any detached prison? Were you all the time in the police detention unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: No, sir. We came out of that prison, but that policeman was -- at 7.00 or 8.00, and we moved over to those facilities where we were put up that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, that is what I am asking you, Witness VV. Can you say that that was not the police detention facility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say yes or no, but what I do know is that they were members of the Convicts Battalion who, during the first 12 days, were entering there when they ill-treated me and provoked me and battered me. Later on, it changed, and I've already said so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, that is what I'm asking you. You told my learned friend today that that is how they entered the police station. So what would then prevent them -- if that is so, what would then prevent them to do the same thing at that other place? Don't you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Unfortunately, we could not hear the witness's answer because they both speak at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: My question was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We did not hear the witness's answer because the questions and answers mingled together. Let the witness answer the question first.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, my last question was whether you would agree with me that it could have also been the police detention facility.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Sir, I cannot say yes or no, but from what I heard, there was always a soldier in a many-coloured uniform, that is, in a camouflage uniform, not a police uniform, and there was always one such man in front of the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, were there some other detainees with you and your colleague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: There were, but for a very short time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were they members of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: On the twelfth day, when they took me out to apply this electric current to me, it was midnight when they took me back. It was 12.00. And then Bosanac came in, unlocked the cell where my colleague was kept, because we were separated, and transferred me to my colleague's place and there we had to lie down on one bed, and four or five Croatian soldiers were brought and a girl, and a young woman, and they were talking amongst themselves that they had been detained for dealings with weapons, for contraband and things, but they spent there only one night.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You mean they spent there only one night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes. They were there only one night. One of them stayed for a couple of days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, I have to ask you -- you see, I'm not interrupting you and you're answering me, but will you please make your answers as short as possible and will you please focus on what I'm asking you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: But, sir, I have to answer you properly because "yes" or "no" is really not for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, very well. Very well. But please try to make your answers as brief as possible and focus on my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think you have to make -- I think you have to make a pause between the question and the answers, Mr. Krsnik. You really give a difficult time to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness VV, I will now ask you to once again and in detail describe the person whom you heard addressed as Bosanac.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Sir, I have already explained that. I do not think there is any need for me to explain it again. I can do it if the Honourable Court orders me to. I can do it a hundred times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What I meant was the colour of his eyes, how tall he is, if you remember, of course, his hair, his build. That's what I meant. With as much detail as possible, if you can do that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Sir, at that time, please put yourself in my shoes and then tell me what is the colour of somebody's eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes. I understand. I know it is not easy for you, but this is the third time I'm asking you, and if it is too hard on you then we can skip that, but I think that you should be interested in identifying the person who was called Bosanac just for the sake of truth and justice, and I care very much about that and my client cares very much about that. We want to identify that person, if that is possible, because of what he did. I mean he needs to be called to account whoever did that. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Well, that is what it should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And that is why I'm asking if it is not too hard for you to give us some more detail. Of course, if it is too difficult for you, then we will move on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I can't do it. Now you want how tall he was, 185 to 190, strongly -- powerful built man, short, fair hair. That is what I still have in my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So you say "fair hair."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Short hair, very, very short, crewcut hair. Fair, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: When you say fair, you mean fair hair, blond?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer. And whilst they were at it, while they were doing this evil with that induction telephone, did any one of you say "Stop it. Stop it. The old man is on his way."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes. And they said it in a sort of panicky voice and very upset. There was a tape recorder so that one could hear it, and one of them shouted, "I do not know who it is, oh, here comes the old man, get him away," and so they switched me off and took me back to the cellar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We have to wait for the interpretation to end, you know. Can we then agree that my client had absolutely no idea about this nor could he have any idea about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Sir, had it happened to me only once, I might believe that, but for 12 days, during those 12 days, I was several times beaten by those four or five soldiers and, according to my book, the commander had to know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, do you personally know if my client ever found that out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Personally, I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I will ask you to tell me how many times were you personally -- how many times did you see with your eyes Mr. Tuta Naletilic in that building in which you were or around that building or generally once you were there? How many times did you see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Sir, in my statement, I said that I saw him only once, that time when they took me to the office and we were drinking tea and coffee, that is, I did not see him again during my stay in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you then know if Mr. Naletilic was there all the time? Did he ever go into that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, sir, since we were in the cellar and it was dark, unlit space, one could feel when the commander is absent, then there is commotion and noise and then, all of a sudden, everything becomes very quiet and that is how we guess that the commander must have arrived. Whether Mr. Naletilic or somebody else, I do not know, but that is how one could make one's assumptions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you are positive that Mr. Naletilic is the commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: The commander of the Convicts Battalion, is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I don't know of what. That is what you are telling us. The commander of anything.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Sir, everybody knew that in Mostar, from a toddler to the grown-up people, Muslims and Croats: The Convicts Battalion, that's Mladen Naletilic, Tuta. Even small children knew that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much for that answer too. And was that so ever since the days of the war against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Since you mentioned the war against the Serbs, didn't Bosniaks have a high opinion of Tuta and Daja and didn't they always say, "Well, where Tuta and Daja are, we can be calm. We can be at rest." Didn't the Bosniaks point that out invariably?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Sir, I do not know that. I was linked up with those Croats who were in the HVO and whom I knew before and -- who were my friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But tell us, didn't Bosniaks have a very, very high opinion of Tuta because of his contribution to the war against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I do not know that. Don't ask me about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Very well. No, I meant -- I see that you know lots of things, you were into very many things, so I thought that maybe you had heard something about that. I mean when the Prosecutor asked you about Mostar, then you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Well, sir, I live in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. Well, that's why I'm asking you. Witness VV, my client and I, regardless of who that could be, we were both very concerned about your claim because it is really horrible thing. It is really true that for 16 days you were given no water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: No, sir. All we had were empty Coca Cola bottles and we relieved ourselves in them, that is, we urinated into it, and we used it to rinse our mouths with.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Then what did you drink for these 16 days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Please, nothing, sir, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Witness, this man nicknamed General, you said that his nickname was General.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could you describe him to us? I know what you said, but could you please give us another detail, if you can remember, whether you said that he was thin, about 185 tall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Black hair.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You mean truly black hair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes, black hair. He had a crutch.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You mean a crutch, so he was a wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Well, I guess he must have been wounded, which he used to beat me, so that is what stuck in my memory. But he came on a couple of occasions, whereas Bosanac came every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you said that when you were in Mr. Naletilic's office, that his hair was grey, was markedly grey?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, were you to be exchanged for some HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I told you, sir, when Maka Radic came in, that's what he told me. I cannot really say yes or no. I'm telling you only what Mr. Maka Radic told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And -- I see. Now, tell me, did you -- were you ever or did the police or anyone take you to court for questioning? Did anyone tell you that the criminal investigation was being conducted against you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: No, sir, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And to this day, you do not know that the court in Mostar conducted a criminal -- conducted criminal proceedings against you and others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, in the light of your answers, there is -- it would serve no purpose to show you the photographs of Siroki Brijeg because apart from the police station, you wouldn't be able to identify them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: No, sir, I couldn't really say anything with certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, that man nicknamed Splico, did he have the same kind of emblem as those you saw at Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Counsel, sir, I cannot say that because at the moment when I was arrested, Kolobara approached me, doused me with petrol. My hands were tied behind my back and he sprinkled my face with petrol.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Only you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes, only me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And only your face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes, only my face. At that was at Dumpor's houses where we were captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm looking at the transcript, you know. In this area, Dumpor's houses, were they already destroyed from the war against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Counsel, these, the houses where we were had already burnt down. It is possible that it was during the hostilities against the Serbs, but it was possible that they were burnt down that day because I was in Mostar at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But when you were there, they were already burnt down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes, but when we were there in front of us, we saw some other houses on fire, looking from there Neretva up towards Raska Gora. These were new flames.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Excuse me, I just had to consult for a moment. Perhaps we did not understand each other. The Dumpor houses, had they already been burned down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Counsel, there are over 40 houses in Rastani and there were only a cluster of five or six there and they had been burned before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You did not see anyone torching houses while you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: While I was there, I did not see it, but as we were coming, the smoke was coming and the flames were there. And Kolobara was walking around with a large container, 10, 15 litre container.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: This was Kolobara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But you did not see him torching anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: No, he just doused me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And was Splico there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did he have any kind of container?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, you told me that there were some civilians there. How were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Counsel, I said that in the statement before this Tribunal that there were three or four in front of them, that I saw one of them in jeans Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and a T-shirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And the others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I don't know, I didn't see them. They were off to the side. This is the one I noticed because he was the closest to me. And sir, I still see that young man on the east side and he has had mental problems ever since.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The one whom you saw in jeans there, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes. I believe he lived in Bijeli Brijeg until the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And the others you never saw nor were they anywhere close to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you now to look please at the statement that is in front of you again and turn to page 2, paragraph 2. "As soon as we were captured on 23 September 1993, Marinko doused me with petrol, intending to set me on fire. However, he first called somebody on the hand-held Motorola radio he was holding in his hand and talked to somebody from Siroki Brijeg. As far as I understood, this person told him that we had to be brought in alive."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Today you said that he first doused you, then called, made the call, and then it was said that it was the old man and then you inferred that it was Tuta. And now I'm going to ask the usher to please hand you this other statement. In fact, you said that you gave both statements in the presence of the ICTY investigators, but this statement is the one that you gave on the 9th of March, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, of course I have all the statements here. I am just going to cover some things with him, so this is why I'm giving him. If you feel that you need your own copies, I have a sufficient number of copies here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you please take the 1998 statement and turn to page -- page 4, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Page 4, paragraph number 5. Did you find that, sir? Which starts like this: "After that, Marinko Kolobara, one of the members of the Convicts Battalion, took a container with gasoline and splashed my face with gasoline, put a lighter close to my face, placed his finger on the button of the lighter but did not push it. At that same moment, Kolobara received an order on the Motorola radio, I think from Tuta, to take us to the Convicts Battalion in Siroki Brijeg," and so on and so forth. Perhaps we should go on and read the next sentence: "Kolobara said that the old man had ordered the prisoners taken to his headquarters, and he referred to Tuta." What I want to ask you is this: The statement you gave in 1998 is at odds with what you said of the one before. You never mentioned Tuta or Daja. You said someone, but here now you said, "I believe -- I think it's Tuta. It's the old man," and so on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Sir, I can explain this to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: He first doused me with petrol and then he approached me to torch me, and then he received a call. I said to Their Honours that I did not know who the old man was at that time. I only learned that in Siroki Brijeg. So this had happened before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: That is fine, but when you gave your statement in 1997, you gave a completely different version. You never mentioned Tuta or the old man by a single word, and you said that before he had doused with petrol that he was already talking on the Motorola.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Sir, I think that that is wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We can read it again.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Go ahead. It is possible that that's how it was stated. It is the wrong sequence. It was a tough situation for me. It is hard to describe it in words.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I understand. I fully understand. But, Witness, you do not mention either Naletilic nor the old man, not a single word. But in the later statement, you said that it was Tuta, and today you gave an explanation that the old man was supposedly Tuta, that you assumed that that is who it was. Do you see the difference?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Sir, I don't know what you want me to say. I said that I learned in Siroki Brijeg, when I was detained, that it was Tuta. At that time, I could not have said that it was Tuta. I did not know who he was talking to. But he then passed on to his soldiers that the old man had ordered that the detainees are to be brought back alive to Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, I appreciate your patience, and I know that it's not easy for you to be in this courtroom today. I completely understand and sympathise with your position, but also please understand me. I'm doing my job. So let us not get excited. It is going to be easier for you too. We'll move faster through this evidence. I only wanted to ask you whether this statement you gave in 1997 and what you told them in 1997 was the truth.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: See? It's very simple. That's all I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Whatever I had stated to the Trial Chamber is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And also what you said in your statements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes, of course. That goes without saying. A lot of time has passed. Years have passed. Maybe the sequence of events, as I said, may not be right, but all the facts are right and correct. This is what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: All I wanted to ask is this, because this statement -- again, let's go to page 2 of the statement from 1997, this second paragraph. And let's not read it again. "Immediately after we were captured ...." Last paragraph on page 1 in the English version. Did you find it, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So, "Marinko doused me with gasoline," and so on, "intending to set me on fire. However, he had talked to somebody from Siroki Brijeg on a Motorola beforehand, and as far as I understood, this person told him that we had to be brought in alive." That's all you said; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Let me explain. Before he set me on fire, he -- after he had doused me and before he set me on fire, he received a call on the Motorola.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I think I understand now. Tell me, on the 23rd of September, how many units were fighting on the side of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And since today you said that you were at Rastani on the 22nd; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You see, you did not mention that in any of your statements, not until today.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Sir, I talked about combat operations, and I never took part in combat operations. On 22nd, I carried food and ammunition, and after the 22nd, the HVO units started attacking Rastani. That was on the 22nd. And I was in Vrapcici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: As an ABiH soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I assume with a rifle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: No. I did not have a rifle. You mean on the 22nd?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: But the line was there on the 22nd.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So this is why I'm asking you. In your estimate, if you can say, how many soldiers of the HVO took part in the fighting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I'm unable to tell you. I can only tell you what I saw, and I cannot really assume things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, this Marinko Kolobara, whom you frequently mention in all your statements, that is in both of the statements, I did not understand well because you gave two different answers to the Prosecutor. [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And Marinko was his relative?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. We've cleared it up. Was Marinko Kolobara also from Vrapcici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Sir, he was from Livac. That is part of Bijelo Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Livac and Vrapcici are next to each other. Excuse me. Just for the record -- I see. Livac is in. Livac is part of Bijelo Polje, and it's adjacent to Vrapcici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: On that day, the 23rd, were you armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you have a Kalashnikov?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: It was a Ciganka, a "gypsy" so-called. It was a JNA issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Just for the record, Ciganka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes. That is sort of a local word for a type of Kalashnikov.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: This is just -- this is just a clarification. ^ Ciganka, is it the same as a Kalashnikov, only manufactured in domestically?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes, in Crvena Zastava.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And your colleague was also armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes. And he had the same -- he was tasked with the same thing. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: That is to bringing ammunition, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I don't know if this was a combat task. I was tasked with bringing ammunition, not taking part in combat. And those who captured us checked the barrels of our weapons and they were clean; in other words, we had not used them to fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you also were wearing ABiH uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So you were in uniform, armed and with backpacks with 750 pieces of bullets, of ammunition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And did you have any grenades?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: As far as I recall --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you not also carry a backpack with grenades?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: No, sir. I may have had one grenade, and I cannot recall about my colleague, but I don't remember us carrying any.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to ask you now --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, 34.3, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: This is going to show Rastani, and I'm going to ask you to help me identify some things. It is going to be fairly difficult to work with this picture because it's elongated, but please take the pointer and let's start with the -- from the point where it says "Exhibit." So will you show to Their Honours and to everyone how far did the ABiH advance until the 20th? You said it was the so-called fly-over or the underpass and then on, all the way out to the power plant so that Their Honours could gain a good picture of what the front line was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: What you can see on this map, you can see this hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You mean all the way to the right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Are you taking us up the hill now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: Yes, up. And it was all along the houses, all the way to the Power Plant Mostar 1 which unfortunately we can't see here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And how far is it from here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to know. The road goes left, right, and around.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, please, I think that here you may be able to mark everything from the underpass to the power plant.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number 34.2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, will you please take a pen and mark how far the ABiH advanced and then maybe you can draw a circle at the power plant.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV
utterances.text: [Marks] Sir, this would be approximately it. There may be some deviations but I mentioned those houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We don't need to be accurate. This is just to get a general picture, and I thank you. Now, can we use the dotted line along -- to mark the Neretva River or mark it with letter N.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we lost the image.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe we did not pay our bill.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps this could be the right moment to actually stop for the day and continue tomorrow because it is 7.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I'm just going to say that. Tomorrow, we'll resume at 2.15 in the Courtroom I. We are adjourned at this moment. Before that, Witness, I have to give you a piece of advice as I did with other witnesses, not to talk to anybody about your testimony today and do not let anybody talk to you about it. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. We will adjourn now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
